title: "Baby, I Can't Use You No More" and "Jealous Woman Like Me"
summary: She explains songs she wrote when angry at her husband Matt and jealous over a woman named Stella.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Well, when we played that "Baby, I Can't Use You No More," --
You had a higher voice that day.
Yeah, that was before I got wet.

See, but I didn't record that song. See, I had made it, see, (unintelligible), I made that song when I was mad at my husband. I say, "I just can't use you no more. I'm going to get me another man." But afterwards, (inaudible).
That was a very fresh song, because you said, "Mama don't want you no more."
Uh-huh, yeah. How did he feel when you sang that song?

He know I was lying. He know I was lying. He knew I wanted him. But I told him ______. But he knew I would want him. (Unintelligible) and so I say, "Yeah, you go on home to your Mama." I say, "I'll go get your clothes." And so (unintelligible). I said, "No, don't go mad. I didn't mean it." But I was (unintelligible) no more. If you're a mean person, sometimes people take his word. You tell people to get out one time too many. See, (unintelligible) one time too many, going to take you at your word because it's always somebody else, it's always somebody else. ______ somebody else.
Now, when you sang "Jealous Woman Like Me," you wrote those words.
Was that for the same man?

(Unintelligible). See, I -- this girl, honey, was jealous. She got to be a nurse. Now, before Stella got to be a nurse, (unintelligible) game she was playing ______. I thought Stella liked me. (Unintelligible) Matt would ______ when I'd come back from my recording, he'd take all my little change and go out and buy Stella all her drinks and things, you know. (Unintelligible). I said,

"Matt, what did you do with so and so and so and so?" "I lost it." You know, because he was gambling, you know. But (unintelligible) bought this gal something, you know, and so (unintelligible). So I was just jealous and didn't believe what he say, you know.
